target: Significant Hobbies public six-app Hub landing

customReplacement.reason: The dependency-free Worker document uses native links, buttons, and semantic sections; no standard interactive component was rebuilt.

contract.purpose: Give the owner one privacy-aware place to understand and open six independently owned personal apps without collapsing their interfaces or source data into one product.
contract.purposeSource: site-health purposeContract for significanthobbies, repository PROJECT_STATUS.md, and the Hub service contract
contract.canonicalPurpose: Significant Hobbies helps its owner coordinate Live, Journal, Calorie, Setline, Kith, and Anchor by exposing a private read-only Hub of typed summaries while each app retains its own interface and data ownership.
contract.audience: The Fleet owner; the public landing also helps a visitor understand which of the six personal apps owns a task.
contract.job: Explain the six-app system, route a visitor to the correct product, and state the private Hub, sync, commercial, and Habits compatibility boundaries honestly.
contract.thesis: A quiet editorial index makes the suite feel like a considered personal system rather than a SaaS bundle or generic application directory.
contract.system: Warm paper, fine ledger rules, Georgia display type, compact sans metadata, monochrome actions, one restrained coral accent, and a responsive grid in the existing dependency-free Worker surface.
contract.signature: The SH 06 ledger index and six numbered product cards turn the exact product count into the page's visual organizing principle.
contract.risk: The large editorial headline is deliberately dominant, but exact 390, 768, and 1440 CSS-pixel captures show the product list, owner-only boundary, and primary actions remain legible without horizontal overflow.

findings: No product-purpose, hierarchy, contrast, interaction, or overflow P0/P1 finding remains in the public landing candidate.

The first nominal 390 screenshot was rejected because macOS headless Chrome rendered at its 500 CSS-pixel minimum and cropped the image. Accepted evidence uses DevTools device metrics and confirms innerWidth, client width, and scroll width are exactly 390 pixels.

answers.product: A shared home and private read-only Hub for exactly six independently owned personal apps.
answers.audience: The owner first, with public visitors using the page to choose which app fits their task.
answers.value: It makes the six products understandable together without turning them into one oversized application.
answers.mechanism: Each source app retains its interface and immediate data while typed summaries and documented actions cross the shared contract boundary.
answers.proof: The first viewport names all six apps and the collection section gives each one an explicit job; the connection and current-state sections state the ownership and sync boundaries.
answers.nextAction: Open the owner-only private Hub or move directly to one of the six product pages; there is no public signup or checkout.

ownerFeedback.note: The owner delegated end-to-end judgment, asked for one-shot high-quality landing pages in SaaSMaker priority order, and explicitly asked not to pause for routine feedback. Production release remains outside this local audit.
